faq_heading: Selling in Abbotsford: your questions answered

blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Written from the City of Abbotsford's own documents: the SSMUH FAQ (July 2024), the SSMUH Application Guide (December 2025), the Zoning Bylaw Updates Overview, the Short-Term Rental Operator's Manual (July 2025) and Business Licence Bylaw 1551-2006, read 2026-11-01. Nothing here states a commission, fee or marketing package; those are for Jared to supply.

Abbotsford is a city of very different lots, from small subdivision lots in the east to large urban lots to farms inside the Agricultural Land Reserve. The same benchmark price does not describe them. What does is the size of your lot, whether it sits inside the Urban Development Boundary, and what the City now lets a buyer add to it.
This page gives the numbers, then the unit rules, suite and garden-suite limits, the short-term rental licence and what I need to price your home.
Abbotsford home prices, September 2026

The MLS® Home Price Index benchmark for a typical Abbotsford home was $701,900 in September 2026, down 9.0% from a year earlier. Detached homes were $1,087,000 (down 11.1% over the year), townhouses $592,600 (down 8.6%) and apartments $370,200 (down 11.0%).

blocks.text: How many units a buyer can build on your Abbotsford lot

The City of Abbotsford says it adopted zoning amendments for the Province's small-scale multi-unit housing rules in June 2024. I have not confirmed the day or the bylaw number, so I have not quoted either. The City's own guidance sets the unit count by lot size.

head: Lot

blocks.source: Source: City of Abbotsford, SSMUH FAQ (July 2024), read 2026-11-01.

blocks.text: The FAQ lists who is left out: lots outside the boundary, lots of 4,050 m² (about one acre) or more, lots with heritage protection and lots inside a Transit-Oriented Area. The December 2025 Application Guide adds that townhouse-zoned lots over 1,120 m² and wider than 35 m have no unit maximum. For a seller, a lot that clears these tests can be priced on what it could hold, and a lot that does not is priced as a home.
Suites, garden suites and coach houses

A single detached house can have one secondary suite, and the City's overview says that in most zones its maximum size is now less than 50% of the principal unit rather than 100 m². The FAQ explains that the BC Building Code lets a suite sit only in a building with one other dwelling unit, so one house cannot hold several suites. A duplex can have one suite per unit.

Garden suites and coach houses are limited to certain zones. The FAQ lists garden suites in RS3-ig, RS7 and N78 and coach houses in SR, RS6-C, RCH and N30, subject to conditions such as lot size. The December 2025 guide caps a garden suite or coach house at 15% of lot area and 100 m². Every accessory unit counts toward the lot's unit total.

blocks.text: If your Abbotsford property is in the Agricultural Land Reserve

The City's December 2025 guide says land in the Agricultural Land Reserve is limited to a principal residence up to 500 m², a secondary suite within it and one additional residence of up to 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less, or up to 186 m² on larger parcels. The multi-unit rules above are not the test for ALR land. If you own acreage, tell me early, because the buyer pool and the financing are different.
Short-term rentals in Abbotsford

Abbotsford requires a business licence. Business Licence Bylaw 1551-2006, Part 11, section 11.30 (added by Bylaw 3675-2025, consolidation last amended July 15, 2025) says a short-term rental must comply with section 140 of the Zoning Bylaw, and before the licence is issued the host provides proof of principal residence, a fire safety plan and a parking plan.

The City's Operator's Manual (July 2025) says a short-term rental must be a business accessory to a residential use in a single detached dwelling or duplex with a secondary suite, garden suite, coach house or accessory farm dwelling unit. It sets a limit of 6 guests in up to 3 bedrooms in urban areas and 8 guests in up to 4 bedrooms in rural and agricultural areas, with at least one extra guest parking space. Proof of principal residence is one BC identity document and at least two supporting documents.

The Province's rule sits on top of anything Abbotsford requires. The Province says the principal residence requirement applies in municipalities with a population of 10,000 or more. A short-term rental can only be the host's usual home, "where they make their home day-to-day," plus one secondary suite or accessory dwelling unit on the same property. A bed and breakfast is allowed only if the owner lives on the property.

Any rental for fewer than 90 consecutive days must also be registered with the Province, one registration number per unit. The Province lists the fee as $100 a year for a host's principal residence and $450 a year for a secondary unit such as a suite or cottage, and compliance with local bylaws is a condition of registration.

faq.q: How many units can a buyer put on an Abbotsford lot?
faq.a: Inside the Urban Development Boundary the City's FAQ gives up to 3 units on a lot of 280 m² or less and up to 4 on a larger one. Up to 6 is possible within 400 m of a frequent bus stop, but the FAQ said no Abbotsford stop met that standard when it was written. Lots of 4,050 m² or more, heritage lots and lots in a Transit-Oriented Area are excluded.

faq.q: How big can a secondary suite be in Abbotsford?
faq.a: The City's overview says that in most zones a secondary suite can now be less than 50% of the principal unit's size, replacing the earlier 100 m² limit. For example, a 240 m² house could have a suite up to 119 m².

faq.q: Where are garden suites and coach houses allowed?
faq.a: The City's FAQ lists garden suites in the RS3-ig, RS7 and N78 zones and coach houses in the SR, RS6-C, RCH and N30 zones, subject to conditions. The December 2025 guide caps either at 15% of lot area and 100 m².

faq.q: Can a buyer run an Airbnb in an Abbotsford house?
faq.a: Only with a City business licence, and only as the host's principal residence in a single detached dwelling or duplex with a suite, garden suite, coach house or accessory farm dwelling unit. The Operator's Manual also limits guests and requires an extra guest parking space, and the Province requires registration.

faq.q: How current are the prices on this page?
faq.a: The benchmark prices come from the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board's MLS® Home Price Index for the month shown. They describe a typical home across Abbotsford, not your house.
